rule: Do not inject completed production directly into combat. Separate physical completion, naval acceptance, carrier trials, unit conversion, carrier allocation and mission readiness.

production_clock.note: Monthly pilot-production centers. November output is not assumed all completed/accepted before 11/26.

physical_existences_by_event_band: approximately 36-42 completed or essentially complete by 1943-11-26; low-confidence production-timing band, not combat strength

event_ready_and_allocatable.reason: Acceptance, carrier qualification, conversion training, spares/tools and deck-specific procedures consume roughly half of raw early-production availability.

mission_allocation_center.reserve_conversion_training: Any additional accepted Kinsei aircraft remain ashore/rear-deck/training or are not mission-ready; do not spawn them into the strike.

zuisei_late_zero.role_note: lower deck/recovery burden, longer safe escort, mature production and carrier procedures

performance_gate.us_system_comparison: Kinsei narrows the individual performance gap and improves climb/closure/rejoin and firepower, but does not erase F6F high-speed/dive/protection/firepower plus radar/CIC/fighter-direction/AA system advantage.

adjudication_delta.old_erroneous_assumption: Kinsei Zero effectively zero in GALVANIC carrier battle due 1943-10-01 ledger wording.
adjudication_delta.corrected_effect: A small but material Kinsei component improves escort persistence/rejoin and CAP interception. It modestly reduces Japanese fighter/attack-aircraft losses and slightly raises weapon-release survival, without changing the centered Lexington/Soryu mission-kill outcome.

anti_overreach: Do not treat 20 Kinsei as equivalent to an all-Kinsei carrier force.
Do not back-port A7M or 1944 production.
Do not convert a higher individual-aircraft performance into US CIC/radar/AA parity.
